 Order No.04 Date: 11.09.2023
1.

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the respondent authorities to distribute the compensation amount among all sons and daughters of the recorded tenant- Nandlal Sahu with respect to the land purchased by the Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) vide sale deed no.392 dated 25.01.2023, as the same is ancestral property of the petitioners and they are the members of Hindu undivided family.
Further prayer has been made for issuance of direction upon the respondent authorities to pay 1/7th share to each co-sharer out of the total compensation amount.

2. Learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the respondent nos.5 to 16 have sold the land appertaining to Mouza Bastacolla, R.S Khata No. 185, R.S Plot No. 521,
measuring an area of 1.86 acres; R.S Plot No. 516, measuring an area of 0.35 acre;
R.S Plot No. 526, measuring an area of 1.65 acres; and R.S Plot No.528 measuring an area of 0.12 acre; total 3.98 acres, to the respondent nos.2 to 4 vide sale deed no.392 dated 25.01.2023 by producing false genealogical table.
3.

It is further submitted that in the last survey record of rights, the said land was recorded in the name of Nandlal Sahu, who died leaving behind four sons, namely, Haribol Swarnkar, Ram Govind Swarnkar, Radholal Swarnkar and Darshanlal Swarnkar and three daughters, namely, Kadam Devi,
Dulari Devi and Subhodhini Devi.

The petitioner no.1 is the daughter of late Kadam Devi; the petitioner no.2 is the son of Late Dulari Devi; and the petitioner no. 3 is one of the sons of Late Subhodhini Devi and as such each petitioner is entitled to 1/7th share out of the total compensation amount with respect to the said land.

4. It is also submitted that the transfer of the said land is in contravention of the Coal Bearing Areas Sakuntla Devi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 11 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23508438/
2 (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957 as well as the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
5.

sentences.text: Per Contra, learned counsel for the respondent-BCCL submits that the said land was purchased by the BCCL on payment of full consideration of Rs.9,85,51,563/- to the vendors and as such the respondent-BCCL is not liable to make payment of any further amount to the petitioners.
The petitioners have raised serious disputed question of fact which cannot be adjudicated in writ jurisdiction.
6. Heard learned senior counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent-BCCL.
This Court has also perused the concerned sale deed brought on record by way of supplementary affidavit dated 04.09.2023.

On bare perusal of the aforesaid sale deed, it appears that the same has been executed by the respondent nos.5 to 16, who are the legal heirs and successors of Haribol Swarnkar, Ram Gobind Swarnkar, Radholal Swarnkar and Darshanlal Swarnkar.

7. This Court is of the view that since the said land has not been acquired rather the same has been transferred to the respondent-BCCL by way of sale deed on payment of full consideration to the respondent nos.5 to 16, there is no question of payment of compensation to the petitioners as prayed by them in the present writ petition.

It is not the case of the petitioners that the respondent nos.5 to 16, who are the vendors of the said land, are strangers, rather they themselves have admitted that the vendors are their co-sharers and each petitioner is entitled to 1/7th share of the compensation amount.

The petitioners have, on the one hand, filed genealogical table showing their names as successors/legal heirs of recorded tenant, namely, Nandlal Sahu, however, on the other hand, they have also filed a copy of new survey settlement record of rights as well as rent receipt with respect to the said land, wherein the names of only Haribol Swarnkar, Ram Govind Swarnkar, Radholal Swarnkar and Darshanlal Swarnkar have been mentioned.
As such, the facts asserted in the present writ petition cannot be treated as undisputed so as to entertain the same.

8. So far as the argument of learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner to the effect that the transfer of the said land in favour of the BCCL is in contravention of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957 and the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Prem Singh and Others Vs. Birbal and others, reported in (2006) 5 SCC 353, has held that there is a presumption that a registered document is validly executed and the onus of proof is on the person who leads evidence to rebut the said presumption.

sentences.text: However, the petitioners instead of taking recourse before the competent civil court by challenging the sale deed dated 25th January, 2023 executed by the respondent nos.5 to 16 in favour of the respondent-BCCL, have filed the present writ petition, which cannot be entertained.
9. The writ petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
10. The petitioners are, however, at liberty to take appropriate recourse before the competent court of civil jurisdiction against execution of the sale deed dated 25th January, 2023.
